Why do so many Indian cities have a Civil Lines? Delhi, Prayagraj, Nagpur, Jaipur and Kanpur all do. 🏛️
Because the British planned many Indian cities as three towns: the old city, the cantonment for soldiers, and Civil Lines for the officers who ran the district, kept apart from both, with big bungalow compounds on wide, tree-lined roads.
In Allahabad (Prayagraj), the Civil Lines was laid out in 1858, months after the 1857 revolt, on eight villages, and was India's biggest town-planning job before New Delhi. In Delhi, Civil Lines housed the officials until New Delhi was built; the Viceroy moved out in 1930.
